newsitem.title: USA: Anonymous benefactor for Grand Forks flood victims.
newsitem.headline: Anonymous benefactor for Grand Forks flood victims.

text.p: An anonymous benefactor apparently touched by the suffering caused by the raging Red River is giving $2,000 payments to thousands of people displaced by flooding, officials said Tuesday.

Grand Forks Mayor Pat Owens and East Grand Forks, Minnesota, Mayor Lynn Stauss together passed out $300,000 worth of $2,000 checks from the "immediate aid fund" to flood victims living at an Air Force Base hangar converted into a shelter.
"The story has touched this individual -- who wants to remain anonymous," Minnesota Public Works spokeswoman Cathy Clark said.

Large sections of Grand Forks, with 50,000 residents, and its sister city East Grand Forks, with a population of 9,500, were submerged more than a week ago by the swollen Red River, and the water had yet to subside completely. Cleanup efforts were just under way and most residents remained under a dusk to dawn curfew.
Any head-of-household who had to evacuate and whose home suffered flood damage would be eligible for the $2,000 payment, Clark said. The benefactor's generosity could amount to millions of dollars.

Both mayors spoke to the anonymous donor by telephone earlier Tuesday and said the person wanted to provide immediate help prior to the infusion of government money and the red tape that comes along with it.
President Clinton has pledged $788 million in aid to three plains states affected by devastating spring floods, but damage to Grand Forks alone may amount to $1 billion.
